id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.topology_type: 2.5D on-package memory: a 3D-stacked DRAM (8-Hi/12-Hi) on a base/logic die, connected to a host compute die through a 1024-bit-wide, 16-channel interface over a silicon interposer. The stack uses TSV + microbumps internally; the interposer carries the data links between memory and host.

supported_topologies.name: Single stack beside host on interposer
supported_topologies.description: One HBM3 stack adjacent to one host die on a shared 2.5D silicon interposer; 1024 data links.

supported_topologies.name: Multiple stacks around a host
supported_topologies.description: Four to six HBM3 stacks around one GPU/accelerator for multi-TB/s aggregate bandwidth (e.g. ~4.9 TB/s with six 24 GB stacks).

supported_topologies.name: Stack-on-host (3D)
supported_topologies.description: Memory die stacked directly on the CPU/GPU chip as an alternative to side-by-side 2.5D.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Bus master for all 16 channels; drives command/address, clock, write data + WDQS; sinks read data + RDQS; performs RFM and RAS handling.
Target; each channel independently decodes commands, manages banks/bank-groups, performs on-die ECC, and reports temperature/alerts.

fields.interconnect_role: The interconnect is physical (TSV + microbump + 2.5D silicon interposer), not a protocol-layer router/bridge. The interposer fans the 1024 wide links between the stack and host over short distances and carries no protocol intelligence.

ordering_guarantees.within_a_channel: Commands committed on rising CK edges; data follows at deterministic latency; row and column buses operate in parallel.
ordering_guarantees.across_channels: No ordering guarantee — the 16 channels are completely independent and not necessarily synchronous.
ordering_guarantees.within_a_channel_pseudo_channels: The two 32-bit pseudo-channels run independent column streams.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: HBM3 is pure memory; the address space is the DRAM array organized into 16 channels, each with bank-groups/banks/rows/columns. No peripheral register region beyond per-channel mode registers.

device_classification.host_gpu_accelerator: Bus master; integrates the HBM3 controller + PHY (e.g. NVIDIA H100).
device_classification.hbm3_stack: Target memory device on the interposer.
device_classification.base_logic_die: Bottom die hosting test/repair/RAS logic and the microbump interface to the interposer.
device_classification.silicon_interposer: 2.5D substrate carrying the 1024 data links between stack and host.

default_signal_values_evidence_tables: Interface section — channels independent and not necessarily synchronous; 64-bit channel at double data rate.
Technology section — TSV, microbumps, silicon interposer, 1024 data links per stack.
HBM3 section — 16 channels of 64 bits, total 1024 data pins, up to 6.4 Gb/s/pin, up to 819 GB/s per stack.
